verdict.rationale: Codex ships an official plugin-building framework — the `@plugin-creator` skill scaffolds the `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` manifest and wires up MCP servers, and OpenAI's own GitHub repo (openai/plugins) provides worked examples (Figma, iOS, web apps, Expo, Notion) plus CLI tooling (`codex plugin marketplace add`) for building and testing plugins, which functions as a de facto SDK/toolkit for extending Codex. However nothing in the pack is explicitly branded or documented as an 'SDK' (e.g., a client library with API bindings), and independent corroboration is thin — community commentary focuses on skills vs MCP tradeoffs rather than confirming a robust developer-SDK experience. Missing for 10: an explicit official SDK/library artifact (not just manifest+CLI), broader third-party hands-on validation of building non-trivial plugins.
